fieldValues.title: check-rfc-integration.mjs cannot see an RFC .md that has no rfc stub record at all
fieldValues.summary: The integration gate only checks manifest-token consistency for RFCs that already have a com.semanticops.spec/rfc record (REQUIRES_INTEGRATION gates on the record's lifecycleState). An RFC whose .md exists in rfcs/ but was never given a stub record is invisible to the gate entirely — no failure, no warning. This is exactly how RFC-005 stayed Draft with fully-implemented, cited-by-name normative content for months (srs#288): every check ran green because there was no record for it to check. srs#288's own acceptance criteria named this same hardening gap as a follow-up rather than a blocking requirement, so it was not closed by that unit.
evidence: srs#288: RFC-005 fully folded into relation-type.json, package-manifest.json, package-bundle.json, the Core/Extension conformance requirements mechanisms, and I-88 — all citing it by name — yet had zero com.semanticops.spec/rfc records and zero check-rfc-integration.mjs diagnostics before this unit created one
scripts/check-rfc-integration.mjs's per-RFC checks all iterate over existing rfc records (resolvers pulled from loadInstances); an .md with no record is simply never visited

rfcs/ contains one file per RFC number as the numbering registry (.claude/commands/rfc.md Stage 2a), so a cross-check (every rfc-NNN-*.md has exactly one rfc record with a matching rfc_number) is mechanically expressible without a new data model concept
fieldValues.body: Proposed hardening (not attempted here — out of scope for srs#288, which only needed RFC-005's own record): add a check to check-rfc-integration.mjs (or a sibling script wired into scripts/checks.json) that lists rfcs/rfc-*.md files, extracts each NNN, and fails if no com.semanticops.spec/rfc record's rfc_number matches. This closes the exact blind spot that let RFC-005 go unnoticed and would need a numbering-registry read plus a diagnostic, no new record type or field.
